CHIEF COMPLAINT
Difficulty with asthma during sports and mood concerns

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a student with asthma triggered by aerobic activity. He attempted to join water polo but experiences difficulty breathing during matches. He has to stop and sit down to use his albuterol inhaler. He describes symptoms including phlegm building up in throat, coughing, chest tightness, wheezing, and lightheadedness. He uses albuterol inhaler 2 puffs for symptom relief, which helps with the phlegm sensation and improves within about 15 minutes, but he still needs to sit down. He experiences shakiness as a side effect from the inhaler. Symptoms occur almost every time he does aerobic exercise or running. He also coughs when around smoke. He denies nighttime asthma symptoms. He is not currently on any daily medications for asthma.

Additionally, patient reports new mood symptoms starting this year. He describes feeling stressed out related to SATs and AP classes. He reports feeling a lot of pressure, episodes of being really down, lack of motivation, not wanting to go out with friends, preferring to stay home, and feeling really tired. He attributes this to school expectations and stress.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient endorses seasonal allergies and fatigue. Denies nighttime asthma symptoms.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Not discussed.

MEDICATIONS
Albuterol inhaler as needed

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient is interested in sports, particularly water polo. He is in school with upcoming SATs and AP classes. He reports significant academic stress.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Heart: sounds good. Lungs: sound good. Eyes: okay. Ears: small amount of fluid noted. Mouth and throat: fine, no tonsils. Abdomen: normal on auscultation and palpation. Reflexes: all normal.

RESULTS
Not discussed.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Asthma: Start Singulair as daily medication. Continue albuterol inhaler as needed. Sit down for a little bit after using inhaler. Should see improvement within about one month. Follow up in 6 weeks.

Mood: Refer to therapist. Will perform screening questionnaires. Follow up in a couple of weeks.
